title: Index union/concat loses non-inferable freq (CustomBusinessDay) depending on input order; restore by validating once on the final index
answers: pd.concat of series with CustomBusinessDay index loses freq
DataFrame from dict of Series has freq=None depending on column order
why does union of DatetimeIndex drop freq
concat result freq depends on order of inputs
body:
Symptom: pd.concat([s1, s3, s2], axis=1) or pd.DataFrame({dict of Series}) gives an index with freq=None, but the same inputs in another order keep the freq. Shows up with offsets that can't be inferred from the values, e.g. CustomBusinessDay(holidays=...).
Root cause: pandas/core/indexes/api.py:union_indexes unions the indexes two at a time. When an intermediate union isn't contiguous, DatetimeIndex._union falls back to the generic set path and calls _with_freq("infer"). Inference can't recover a custom offset, so freq becomes None and stays None.
Fix pattern: don't try to keep freq at each pairwise step. Validate once, on the final combined index, with pandas/core/indexes/api.py:_maybe_restore_freq. It is called in the union_indexes "special" branch and after safe_sort_index in _get_combined_index. It runs type(result._data)._validate_frequency(result, freq) and re-attaches freq only if the final values conform. Nothing is inferred.
Constraints: it only acts when the result is a DatetimeIndex or TimedeltaIndex with freq None, the result is monotonic increasing, and every input has the same non-None freq. Results that aren't monotonic (sort=False) or have a real gap (e.g. a tz DST case such as America/Santiago) correctly keep freq=None. If you add a new place where a combined index becomes final, call this helper there too.
applies: pandas/core/indexes/api.py index combining used by concat, the DataFrame constructor and align
